- Diffusion‑step experiments show that 4 steps achieve 0.990 accuracy in 66 ms, essentially the same as 6 steps (0.990 in 74 ms), indicating a potential latency win.

## [2026-06-12 15:05] — double-decoder efficiency improvements: talker step fraction + consensus voting; double now wins time-to-90% everywhere

**TL;DR:** Two efficiency features added to tests/double_decoder.py (commits 3df51bd, cadd490, default flip below): (1) talker_steps_fraction trains the fast-converging talker on a fraction (default now 0.25) of the thinker's steps, cutting the double decoder's sequential training tax from ~2.0x to ~1.25x per step; (2) consensus_vote_decode stops sampling candidates once every row's modal answer has consensus_min_agree=3 votes. Result: the double decoder now beats the baseline on real time-to-90% in all four cells where it previously lost three — 3d: 4.43/3.29 s vs 5.48/4.06 s; 5d: 7.77/6.37 s vs 11.12/21.44 s — with full accuracy parity at 5d/1200 (1.000/0.998 vs the prior 1.000/0.998). Consensus voting: 404.6 ms vs 671.3 ms full vote (1.66x faster, 5 of 8 candidates used), accuracy 0.982 vs 0.984. Diffusion steps 4 ≈ 6 in accuracy (0.990 both) at 66.0 vs 74.2 ms. 27 tests pass, pyaot clean.

**Long description:** Rationale from the 14:20 entry: the talker's oracle accuracy is 1.000 from very early in training, so equal step budgets waste talker compute. talker_steps_for(config, steps) = max(1, round(steps * fraction)); run_experiment trains the talker with a fraction-scaled config copy; time_to_target scales each talker round. consensus_vote_decode tracks per-row answer counts in plain dicts, samples up to candidate_count thoughts, breaks when all rows have a modal count >= consensus_min_agree, returns (votes, candidates_used). Proving tests written first (4): fraction math incl. floor, early stop at exactly 2 with temperature-0 identical candidates, cap at candidate_count when consensus unreachable, run_experiment smoke with fraction. Verbatim measurement rows: {"time_to_90_frac25", 3d, seeds 20260612/7: double 4.43/3.29 s (400/300 steps) vs baseline 5.48/4.06 s (400/300)}; {5d: double 7.77/6.37 s (500/400) vs baseline 11.12/21.44 s (600/1100)}; {"acc_frac25_5d1200": double 1.0/0.998, vote 0.998/0.998, oracle 1.0/1.0}; {"diffusion_steps" on 5d/1200 models: 3 -> 0.988 @ 55.4 ms, 4 -> 0.990 @ 66.0 ms, 6 -> 0.990 @ 74.2 ms}; {"vote_compare_5d": full 0.984 @ 671.3 ms, consensus 0.982 @ 404.6 ms, used 5}. After parity confirmation, talker_steps_fraction default flipped 1.0 -> 0.25; 27 tests still pass, make pyaot clean. Comparison to the 14:20 baseline numbers: 3d double improved 7.4/8.0 -> 4.43/3.29 s; 5d 23.83/11.54 -> 7.77/6.37 s; baseline numbers unchanged within noise as expected.

**What worked:** Both levers. The fraction attacks exactly the measured bottleneck (two-model sequential cost); consensus voting converts the vote's fixed 8x into an adaptive ~5x at converged quality. The diffusion-step probe shows step 4 is the latency sweet spot, a further free ~11% on greedy double inference if adopted.

**What failed:** Nothing in this unit. Note consensus used 5 candidates (not the minimum 3) because temperature-1.0 sampling on 500 rows needs a few extras before every row reaches 3 agreeing answers; per-row freezing (stop computing rows already consensual) would cut deeper but complicates batching — not implemented.

**What was kept / discarded:** Kept both features, 4 proving tests, docs entries, the 0.25 default. diffusion_steps default left at 6 (the 4-step gain is within single-run noise; adopt only after a multi-seed check).

**Open questions / next steps:** (1) Per-row consensus freezing for deeper inference savings. (2) talker_steps_fraction below 0.25 untested — the floor of the talker's required budget is unknown. (3) diffusion_steps=4 default pending multi-seed verification. (4) Parallel thinker/talker training remains the biggest untapped lever (GPU still fully occupied this session).
